NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a coordinated parameter/procedure regimen — lower cryolite ratio, elevated CaF2, increased ACD, and a slowed start-up ramp — that jointly reduces sodium activity in the bath and the sodium reduction flux at the cathode during the critical early-campaign window when penetration initiates. Standard practice holds CR ~2.35, CaF2 ~4.5%, ACD at design minimum, and ramps at maximum safe rate; this regimen moves all four levers simultaneously in the sodium-suppression direction, which standard practice does not do because each lever is normally optimized for current efficiency or throughput alone. Adjacent-technique clearance: the closest existing practice is "low-sodium bath" operation in some Chinese smelters (CR 2.1–2.2, CaF2 5–6%) but it is applied as a steady-state recipe without the coordinated ACD increase and the dedicated slow-ramp start-up procedure; the departure is the JOINT SCHEDULE of all four levers during the first 30–60 days, not any single setpoint.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: sodium penetration flux J_Na ∝ a_Na · exp(-E_a/RT) · i_cathode, where a_Na is sodium activity in bath, i_cathode is cathodic current density. Lower CR (higher AlF3) reduces a_Na; CaF2 forms NaF·CaF2 complexes further reducing free a_Na; increased ACD lowers i_cathode at fixed line current; slower ramp reduces thermal stress cracking that opens penetration paths. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = sodium penetration flux into cathode carbon; the mechanism moves it DOWN by (1) reducing a_Na via CR 2.15 + CaF2 6.5% (Δa_Na/a_Na ≈ -30% from published bath models), (2) reducing i_cathode via ACD +8 mm (Δi/i ≈ -7% at 350 kA), (3) eliminating thermal-shock microcracks via 7-day ramp vs standard 3-day (crack density reduction >50% from plant data). This REDUCES the failure driver. Magnitude verification: combined effect targets >40% reduction in sodium uptake rate (validated by cathode core drilling at 30/60/90 days vs baseline cells).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
| Item | Description | Tag | Location / Parameter |
|------|-------------|-----|----------------------|
| 1 | Cryolite ratio setpoint change: 2.35 → 2.15 | (c) | DCS bath-chemistry setpoint table (existing) |
| 2 | CaF2 target concentration change: 4.5% → 6.5% | (c) | DCS bath-chemistry setpoint table (existing) |
| 3 | ACD setpoint change: design minimum → design minimum + 8 mm | (c) | Anode lifting system setpoint (existing) |
| 4 | Metal-pad height setpoint: nominal → nominal + 5 mm (to maintain bath level) | (c) | Metal-pad controller setpoint (existing) |
| 5 | Start-up ramp-rate procedure: 3-day full current → 7-day staged ramp (25%/50%/75%/100% at 48h intervals) | (c) | Start-up procedure document (existing) |
| 6 | Alumina feed setpoint: maintain 2.5–3.0% (unchanged, but tightened control band) | (c) | Alumina feeder PID parameters (existing) |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
| Dimension | Standard Practice | This Intervention | Delta |
|-----------|-------------------|-------------------|-------|
| Hardware install | None (parameter changes only) | None | 0 |
| Commissioning | Setpoint updates (routine) | Setpoint updates + procedure doc revision | Same class (shift-supervisor effort) |
| Operation | Standard setpoints | New setpoints + 4-day longer start-up | Operational loss: 4 days × 350 kA × 4.2 V ≈ 1.4 GWh deferred production (priced at ~$80k); NO curtailment during steady state |
| Maintenance | Unchanged | Unchanged | 0 |
| Cost class | Parameter tuning | Parameter tuning + procedure update | Same burden class (no procurement, no tooling, no downtime beyond scheduled start-up) |
Conclusion: SAME burden class. The only priced loss is the 4-day extended start-up (explicitly zero curtailment during steady-state operation).

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Select 4 cells entering start-up this campaign. Apply the full regimen (Items 1–6). Run 4 matched baseline cells on standard practice. Instrumentation: existing DCS logs (bath chemistry, ACD, metal pad, current, voltage), cathode core drilling at 30, 60, 90 days (standard lab capability), collector-bar seal inspection at 90 days (standard shutdown window). Pass/fail thresholds: (1) sodium content in cathode cores ≤ 60% of baseline at 90 days (ICP-MS), (2) heave measured by laser survey ≤ 2 mm vs ≥ 5 mm baseline, (3) zero collector-bar seal cracks at 90 days. Duration: 90 days from start-up. Kill criterion: if any intervention cell shows heave rate > baseline at 30 days, abort and revert to standard setpoints. Falsifies effectiveness: failure rate/magnitude DROPS with intervention.
